resources.string: Check that photos are saved
“Received” means the original arrived in full and passed an integrity check. For a Live Photo, this includes both the photo and its video.
“Saved to the Pixel’s Photos” means a gallery copy exists on this phone. BackupDuck prepares supported motion formats and burst information. The gallery decides whether to group burst photos.

Cloud upload is separate and belongs to Google Photos. Check the account and backup status there, and enable backup for the BackupDuck folder if needed. BackupDuck can’t see whether cloud upload has finished.
Keep receiving in the background
Turn on receiving on the Receive tab before leaving BackupDuck. Android shows a notification while it runs. Allow notifications if the system asks.
Battery restrictions can interrupt background reception. Check BackupDuck’s battery restrictions in this Pixel’s system settings. A ready Pixel can’t keep the sending device running.

iOS decides how much background time an iPhone gets, so continuous transfer while locked isn’t guaranteed. Keep BackupDuck open for a large first transfer. On a Mac, keep the app running and the computer awake.
Free up space on this Pixel
Google Photos decides which phone copies it can remove with “Free up space”, based on its own backup checks. This doesn’t remove originals kept inside BackupDuck.

“Free up space after saving to Photos” in Storage checks the gallery copy before removing BackupDuck’s copy. Missing, changed or unverified copies keep their originals. Turning this off can’t restore removed files or confirm cloud upload.
Keeping originals lets BackupDuck retry a failed save to Photos. A converted motion photo isn’t an exact archive of the original photo and video.
Connect another iPhone or Mac
Put both devices on the same Wi-Fi network, where they can reach each other. Choose Connect a new device on Receive, then choose the device to connect.
For an iPhone, use the iPhone to scan the code on this Pixel. For a Mac, show the code on the Mac and scan it with the Pixel. Camera access is needed only for scanning.
Choosing a connection method starts receiving. Once ready, BackupDuck shows a code or opens the scanner. Check the device names on both sides after connecting.
An iPhone or Mac can’t connect
Make sure both devices use the same Wi‑Fi and can reach each other. Guest networks or a VPN can block a connection even when the network name is the same.
If the Pixel can’t start receiving, its Wi-Fi address may be unavailable or another app may be using the connection. Return to Receive and follow the reason shown there.
A photo wasn’t saved to Photos
Open Needs you on the Photos tab to see the cause, then retry saving. Starting a retry doesn’t mean the photo has been saved.
If the original arrived in full, BackupDuck can use it to retry without sending it again. If the transfer itself failed, check the cause and retry controls on the iPhone or Mac.

For help, export a report from Diagnostics at the bottom of Settings. Include when the issue happened and whether both apps were open. Reports contain no photos or connection codes; review them before sharing.
Storage is full and receiving paused
Open Storage to see what uses this Pixel’s capacity. Gallery copies, originals kept by BackupDuck and temporary conversion files all need space.
The original-storage budget and free-space reserve both limit new reception. Raising the original budget doesn’t create free space on the phone.

Follow the guidance in Storage to free space, or export originals you want to keep first. While receiving is running, photos waiting for space are checked again automatically. Repeated imports don’t fix a full phone.
Receiving stopped
If you stopped receiving yourself, turn it on again on Receive. Battery or background limits can also interrupt it. Open BackupDuck to continue when prompted.

After a Pixel restart, BackupDuck restores receiving when Android allows it. On Android 15 or later, tap the notification or open the app to continue. Received records and unfinished transfers are kept.

To update, open About BackupDuck in Settings and check for updates. If Android reports a different installation source or signature, keep the existing app. Uninstalling or clearing storage may lose originals kept inside BackupDuck.
Auto cleanup didn’t run

Check the Auto cleanup row in Storage. It shows the next step if the account needs confirmation, Accessibility access is off or the last result needs your review. Cleanup must be set up and turned on before it can run automatically.

Auto cleanup uses Accessibility to tap “Free up space” in Google Photos. Google Photos decides which phone copies can be removed. BackupDuck can’t see cloud upload results; when asked, check in Google Photos and return to confirm.
If it still can’t finish, export a report from Diagnostics at the bottom of Settings for help. Review its contents before sharing.
